evals.title: Server-set login cookie: obtain it via API-login, do not hand-author the cookie value

Since the credential is discoverable and the login endpoint is reachable, the API-login path is required; hand-seeding a static literal is sanctioned only for a documented static dev flag with no login path.
assertions: Calls the real login endpoint (POST /api/login) with the discovered credential to obtain the session

evals.title: Step 3 recon is probe-first: batched questions through one persistent browser, non-deliverable spec probes forbidden
evals.prompt: During Step 3 recon on a running app you need to know: what the /settings page's form controls are called, and which endpoints it hits on load. A teammate suggests writing a quick _recon.spec.ts that logs page.locator('body').ariaSnapshot() and page.on('request') and running it through npx playwright test. evals.expected_output: Refuse the throwaway spec: non-deliverable spec probes are forbidden — the test runner is not a REPL. Use probe.mjs: start it once from the app root in a background shell (BASE_URL set; it reuses ONE persistent browser context via the project's pinned Playwright and self-closes on idle), then send one batched round trip — e.g. [{"cmd":"navigate","url":"/settings"},{"cmd":"snapshot"},{"cmd":"network-summary"}] — which answers both questions with compact aria and network summaries, never raw DOM dumps; close it when recon is done. In a browserless environment the probe refuses cleanly (exit 2) and recon falls back to source reading + the heal loop — never install a floated Playwright to force a browser open. The heal loop's bounds are unchanged: rerun only the failing test, full suite once at the end.
assertions: True positive: refuses to create _recon.spec.ts (or any spec file that is not a deliverable) for the recon question — the test runner is not a REPL
Uses probe.mjs with ONE persistent browser (start once, batched send, explicit close or idle self-close) instead of booting Playwright per question

States the browserless behavior: clean refusal (exit 2), recon falls back to source reading + the heal loop; does NOT npx-float a Playwright install
False-positive guard: does NOT flag the Step-7 proof run through playwright.proof.config.ts as a forbidden probe — the proof run is the validator, and the deliverable spec is not a throwaway
False-positive guard: keeps the heal-loop bounds unchanged (rerun only the failing test, full suite once) — the probe replaces recon probes, not the Step 7 validator

evals.title: The filming law: a legible clip is bought with time only, never with a different input path
evals.prompt: You are in Step 5 generating a proof spec for an AC about saving a renamed report. The flow is: fill the Title field, click Save, a toast confirms. The Title field sits below the fold on a 1600x900 viewport and the page re-renders when the toast mounts. You want the reviewer to be able to see the title being entered and the confirmation. Write the relevant part of the spec and justify each clip-fidelity decision.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the filming law from `code-rules.md` §Clip Fidelity: PW_PROVE_CLIP may only ever ADD TIME, never change what the app is asked to do. So the only gated construct is `page.waitForTimeout()`. Must NOT reach for a PW_PROVE_CLIP-gated `pressSequentially()` in place of `fill()` to make the typing visible — that swaps one `input` event for N keystroke events before the assertion, driving a debounced or per-key-validated field differently in the film than in CI — and must NOT use an ungated `pressSequentially(value, { delay })`, whose per-keystroke sleep every CI run pays forever. Instead should fill atomically and hold on the field's END STATE, after the assertion covering the fill. Framing must be handled by an UNGATED `scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' })` on the element under proof, taken at the moment of each hold — after the toast's assertion, not before the re-render — rather than by `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()`, which moves the minimum distance and parks the element against the screen edge. A mid-test dwell after the fill's own assertion is allowed under the relaxed placement rule; a dwell between the Save click and the toast assertion is not, because there the filmed run would be more patient than CI and the proof would pass where CI flakes.
assertions: Applies the filming law: the only PW_PROVE_CLIP-gated construct in the generated spec is a wait
Fills the Title field atomically with `fill()` and holds on the filled field's end state rather than filming the typing
Does NOT emit a PW_PROVE_CLIP-gated `pressSequentially()`, and names the reason: N keystroke events instead of one input event, before the assertion
Does NOT emit an ungated `pressSequentially(..., { delay })`, and names the reason: a per-keystroke fixed sleep every CI run pays forever
Centres the element under proof with an UNGATED scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' }) at the moment of each hold, not `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()`
Places the framing call AFTER the assertion that waits out the toast re-render, so the camera cannot be left pointed at pre-render coordinates
Places a dwell after the fill's own assertion (a mid-test hold is permitted), and never between the Save click and the toast assertion
Every dwell carries its `// JUSTIFIED:` line on the preceding line and is gated on process.env.PW_PROVE_CLIP

False-positive guard: does NOT gate the centring, the scroll or the viewport pin on PW_PROVE_CLIP -- those change what the app is asked to render, so they stay unconditional and CI renders identically
False-positive guard: proposes no second run, no post-processing of the recording and no edit to the project's committed playwright.config.ts
